title: Unlocking the Power of Diffusion Models in Sequential Recommendation: A Simple and Effective Approach

problem.claim: Existing diffusion-based sequential recommendation models suffer from embedding collapse.

gap.claim: Existing methods have limitations in capturing both sequence dynamics and item representations.

contributions.claim: ADRec applies an independent noise process to each token and performs diffusion across the entire target sequence during training.
ADRec combines auto-regression for token interdependency with token-level diffusion for per-token distributions.
ADRec uses a three-stage training strategy and denoises only the last token during inference.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that ADRec overcomes limitations of existing methods in capturing sequence dynamics and item representations.
The authors report comprehensive empirical evaluation across six datasets showing improved accuracy and efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper focuses on embedding collapse in diffusion-based sequential recommendation models.
ADRec uses independent per-token noise and sequence-wide diffusion during training.
The framework combines autoregressive token interdependency modeling with token-level diffusion.
A three-stage training strategy is introduced to further mitigate embedding collapse.
Inference denoises only the last token, and experiments are reported across six datasets.
